title: Responsible Alcohol Service & Spotting Intoxication
blurb: The legal duty not to serve drunk guests, how to spot the signs, and how to refuse service with tact.
siteNotes: Where the refusals log is kept and how an entry is written
How taxis are arranged for guests at the venue
Who the duty manager is on each shift
legalNotes: Selling alcohol to someone who is drunk is an offence under the Licensing Act 2003, s.141. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2003/17/section/141 (wording in the trainer is general; section number from general knowledge, not re-checked this session).
CHECK: the trainer's "record any refusal in the log" is venue practice rather than a legal requirement; confirm the venue keeps a refusals log and where.
CHECK: the trainer says "protects our licence"; confirm the venue is content with this wording alongside its premises licence conditions.

cards.kicker: Bar and front of house · 10 minutes
cards.title: Responsible Alcohol Service & Spotting Intoxication
cards.body:
By the end of this session you can:
- spot the signs that a guest has had enough
- refuse service tactfully and look after their welfare
- know when to call a manager and record a refusal

cards.title: It is the law, and it keeps people safe
cards.body: Serving alcohol responsibly is a legal duty and a big part of keeping our guests safe. It is against the law to sell alcohol to someone who is already drunk, and it is on us to spot when someone has had enough and handle it well.

cards.title: Learn the signs
cards.body: It is a judgement call. It is better to notice early and slow things down than to wait until there is a problem.

cards.title: Be tactful, be firm but kind
cards.body: Slow down or stop serving them alcohol, and offer water, soft drinks or food. Do it discreetly, without embarrassing them. A friendly, respectful approach is far more likely to be accepted.

left.title: Do
items: Offer water, soft drinks or food

right.title: Do not
items: Let them buy drinks for others

cards.title: Look after them, and get help
cards.body: Never let an intoxicated person buy drinks for others, as that is a way round the refusal. Keep an eye on anyone who seems vulnerable. Help arrange a taxi or a safe way home where you can, and never let someone drink-drive if you can prevent it.

items.title: Get them home
items.text: Taxi or a safe way home.

items.title: Call a manager
items.text: If it escalates or turns aggressive.

items.title: Record
items.text: Note the refusal in the log.

cards.title: Remember
cards.body:
- It is against the law to sell alcohol to someone who is already drunk
- Notice early and slow things down
- Refuse discreetly, and offer water, soft drinks or food
- Never let a drunk guest buy drinks for others, or drive
- Call a manager if it escalates, and record any refusal in the log

cards.q: It is against the law to sell alcohol to someone who is already drunk.
cards.why: It is a legal duty, and it protects the guest, other guests and our licence.

cards.q: Which of these is a sign that someone may be intoxicated?
options: Asking for the menu twice
Asking for a glass of tap water
Slurred or loud speech
Paying with a card
cards.why: Signs include slurred or loud speech, unsteadiness, glazed eyes, becoming argumentative or overly friendly, and fumbling with money.

cards.q: To manage someone who has had too much, you should offer…
options: Water, soft drinks or food
A smaller measure of the same drink
A free shot to take the edge off
Another round on the house
cards.why: Slow down or stop alcohol and offer water, soft drinks or food.

cards.q: You should let an intoxicated person buy drinks for their friends.
cards.why: That is a way round the refusal, so never let it happen.

cards.q: How should you refuse further service?
options: By pointing out how much they have had
By ignoring them until they leave
Loudly, so others see why
Discreetly and respectfully
cards.why: A friendly, respectful approach is far more likely to be accepted and avoids embarrassing the guest.

cards.q: Refusing service to a drunk guest protects them, other guests and our licence.
cards.why: It protects the guest, other guests and the venue's licence.

cards.q: Which of these is one way to look after the welfare of an intoxicated guest?
options: Leave them to sort their own way out
Help arrange a taxi or a safe way home
Let them walk it off in the car park
Give them a coffee, then let them drive
cards.why: Help arrange a taxi or a safe way home, and never let someone drink-drive if you can prevent it.

cards.q: If a situation escalates or someone gets aggressive, you should call a manager.
A refusal of service should be…
options: Mentioned only if the guest complains
Kept to yourself
Recorded in the log
Left for the next shift to find
cards.why: Record any refusal in the log.

cards.q: It is better to notice early and slow things down than wait for a problem.
cards.why: Spotting the signs early lets you handle it tactfully before there is a problem.
